memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "Then the Lord said, "If they do not believe you or pay attention to the first sign, they may believe the second. But if they do not believe these two signs or listen to you, take some water from the Nile and pour it on the dry ground. The water you take from the river will become blood on the ground."" - Exodus 4:8-9 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
God gives a first sign. Then a second, in case the first is not enough. Then a third, in case the first two fail.

Read that again and let it sink in. God knew they might not believe, and He made provision anyway. He is not a God who gives one chance and walks away offended.

There is deep pastoral comfort here. Many of us carry a quiet fear that God is running out of patience with us — that we have doubted too often, fallen too many times, asked too many questions. This verse says otherwise. He knows exactly how slow we are, and He keeps working with us.

That said, patience is not permission. The third sign involves the Nile turning to blood — a warning that persistent refusal has consequences. God is patient, but He is not indifferent.

Peter puts both truths together: the Lord is patient, not wanting anyone to perish (2 Pet 3:9). His patience is an invitation, not an excuse.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Where have I assumed God has run out of patience with me?
2. Is there an area where I have mistaken God's patience for His approval?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Patient Father, thank You for bearing with my slowness to believe. Do not let me take Your kindness for granted. Amen.
